title: a throw of an Error subclass in a Result-returning function lifts into the failure variant
notes: The failure line carries the compiler-stable nominal identity because that is what specification/failures.mdx, 'Error Prototype', says is the key: "Handler selection MUST use compiler-stable nominal identity, not a forgeable user `_tag` or minifier-sensitive constructor name in compiled artifacts." Until 2026-08-25 the shared harness printed `error.constructor.name` — the very thing that sentence names as the wrong key — and this line read `error Boom: bad value -2`. Both backends now mint `smithers:<module path>:<Class>` and produce this line byte-identically. That agreement is the point: three of the four obligations in 'Error Classes' (stable nominal identity, serialization evidence, cross-realm transport metadata) were absent from the Go fork and no corpus case could see it, because `constructor.name` is `Boom` whether or not an identity exists. See conformance/runner/harness.mjs.
